title: IEEE 802.3 MAC (GMII-style byte interface) with address filtering and PAUSE flow control

fields.desc: byte time - 1 in PCLK (both ends of the link alike)

regs.name: MAC
regs.desc: Station address (MAC0 = bits 31:0, MAC1 = bits 47:32; the first byte on the wire is bits 47:40)

regs.name: TX
regs.desc: Transmit byte (DA first; the MAC adds preamble, padding and FCS); a frame starts once its first byte is in TX, and each next byte must arrive within a byte time

regs.name: RX
regs.desc: Received byte (FCS removed); read it within a byte time

fields.desc: a received PAUSE holds the transmitter

irqs.name: TX_UNDERRUN
irqs.desc: a transmit byte was late: the frame was ended with gtx_er

irqs.name: RX_FRAG
irqs.desc: a fragment or a bad preamble was received and dropped

notes: gtxd / gtx_en / gtx_er and grxd / grx_dv / grx_er are the GMII-style line pins; they pass through unchanged.
